slice: WS03 hygiene: disposable session-core DB harness, Docker Desktop recovery script and runbook, Build ledger, and the plan-mode gap decision (design only; nothing created, run or committed)
summary: Read-only design of the three hygiene deliverables, grounded in code read in this worktree. Nothing was written, run or committed, and Docker was not touched. (a) apps/Model Plane/scripts/tests/session-core-db-tests.sh: a loopback-only, per-run Postgres harness pinned to the stack image postgres:16.14-alpine3.24 (deploy/docker-compose.yml:31). Readiness is probed over TCP inside the container. An EXIT trap removes the container and its anonymous volume. It runs cargo test -p session-core --bins -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1 and skips two tests by name (audit_publisher.rs:1549 and :1685 expect NATS_URL and would panic). (b) apps/Model Plane/scripts/dev/docker-desktop-recover.ps1: dry run by default. With -Apply it only stops Docker Desktop processes, runs wsl --terminate docker-desktop, renames two named folders, and restarts Docker Desktop. It never deletes. Plus the runbook. (c) Exact Build ledger text for WS03 S1-S5 (commit hashes checked against git log) and a new decision-ledger entry for the plan-mode gap. The gap is verified by code: in the SPA, agentic implies plan_mode (chat-client.ts:1085, 1117-1121); a plan-mode run is pinned READ_ONLY and rejects risky calls (sse.rs:9027-9028; agent.rs:1845-1867); approveTurnPlan sets the composer back to Ask (use-chat-controller.ts:2077); an approved plan is consumed only by a run that is not in plan mode (sse.rs:9599-9603), which no UI turn sends.
approach: Harness. A fresh container per run, named with PID and RANDOM. It is published with -p 127.0.0.1::5432, not -P: the existing approval-continuation-proof.sh uses -P, which publishes on every interface, and an unpinned postgres:16-alpine. The per-run password comes from od and is never printed. The login probe reads the password from the container's own environment, so it never appears on the host command line. Readiness uses pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 inside the container, because the image's first-run socket-only server would otherwise count as ready. The database is session_core_test, which loop_checkpoint.rs:468 requires to contain 'test'. There is no host-side /dev/tcp probe, since SYSTEM_STATUS.md:815 records that probe hanging on Docker Desktop. cargo runs after cd into rust/, not with --manifest-path, which avoids MSYS path conversion; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 is also set. unset DATABASE_URL ensures an inherited URL is never used. REQUIRE_CONTRACT=1 matches CI. session-core has no sqlx compile-time macros (grep count 0), so migrations run inside each test and the empty database needs no pre-migration step. The Docker engine is checked with docker version and the image with docker image inspect (no surprise pull). Recovery. The dry run only reads, including the VM probe, which runs only when the distro already shows Running. -Apply runs four steps and refuses while docker info answers unless -Force is given. Exit codes are 0, 1, 2 and 3. Process names are matched by regex and Docker Desktop.exe is searched in two candidate paths. The refusal path is safe to test on a healthy machine. Runbook. Symptoms from the 2026-10-17 facts, bounded read-only diagnosis, the fix, a do-not list, orphan detection, and prevention. The plan itself tells people to run Linux-gated Rust tests in a rust:1 container on Windows (plan lines 1106 and 2108). That is a likely origin of the orphan, stated as unconfirmed. Docs. Each slice carries a verification level (source-verified, live-verified, or not yet recorded). The S5 live proof is recorded, but no artifact exists in the tree, and the entry says so. The decision entry is proposed, cites file:line for every claim, and marks names that do not yet exist in the tree as planned.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run the Session Core Postgres-backed tests against a throwaway Postgres
# container that exists only for this run. It never touches the running stack
# (model-plane-postgres-1), never reads a stack credential, and never prints the
# per-run password or the DATABASE_URL. The container is bound to loopback on a
# random host port; the EXIT trap removes it with its anonymous volume on
# success, on failure and on Ctrl+C.
#
# Usage: session-core-db-tests.sh [test-name-filter ...]
#   e.g. session-core-db-tests.sh loop_checkpoint tool_ledger
#
# Needs a responding Docker engine and the image below present locally.
# If the engine is wedged, see apps/Model Plane/docs/runbooks/docker-desktop-recovery.md.

# Git Bash must not rewrite POSIX-looking arguments for native programs.
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
# This run uses only its own database, never one inherited from the shell.
unset DATABASE_URL

# Must match the image the stack runs (apps/Model Plane/deploy/docker-compose.yml).
IMAGE="postgres:16.14-alpine3.24"
PG_USER="session_core"
PG_DB="session_core_test"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
RUST_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/rust"
CONTAINER="session-core-dbtest-$$-${RANDOM}${RANDOM}"
PG_PASSWORD="$(od -An -N24 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
CLEANUP_NEEDED=0

cleanup() {
  if [[ "$CLEANUP_NEEDED" == 1 ]]; then
    docker rm -f -v "$CONTAINER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

for tool in docker cargo od tr sed seq; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    echo "BLOCKED $tool is unavailable" >&2
    exit 2
  }
done
[[ -f "$RUST_DIR/Cargo.toml" ]] || {
  echo "BLOCKED $RUST_DIR/Cargo.toml not found" >&2
  exit 2
}
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}' >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "BLOCKED the Docker engine does not answer; see docs/runbooks/docker-desktop-recovery.md" >&2
  exit 2
}
docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "BLOCKED $IMAGE is not present locally; pull it deliberately first" >&2
  exit 2
}

# Set before docker run, so a container that was created but failed to start is removed too.
CLEANUP_NEEDED=1
docker run -d \
  --name "$CONTAINER" \
  -e POSTGRES_USER="$PG_USER" \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD="$PG_PASSWORD" \
  -e POSTGRES_DB="$PG_DB" \
  -p 127.0.0.1::5432 \
  "$IMAGE" >/dev/null

PORT_LINES="$(docker port "$CONTAINER" 5432/tcp)" || {
  echo "BLOCKED Docker published no host port for the disposable Postgres" >&2
  exit 2
}
PORT="$(printf '%s\n' "$PORT_LINES" | sed -n '1s/.*://p')"
[[ -n "$PORT" ]] || {
  echo "BLOCKED Docker published no host port for the disposable Postgres" >&2
  exit 2
}

# Probe over TCP inside the container: during first-time initialisation the image
# runs a socket-only server, which must not count as ready.
ready=0
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if docker exec "$CONTAINER" pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U "$PG_USER" -d "$PG_DB" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [[ "$ready" != 1 ]]; then
  echo "BLOCKED disposable Postgres did not become ready; last log lines follow" >&2
  docker logs --tail 20 "$CONTAINER" >&2 2>&1 || true
  exit 2
fi

# The password comes from the container's own environment, not from this host command line.
docker exec "$CONTAINER" sh -c 'PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -tAc "select 1"' >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "BLOCKED disposable Postgres rejected the probe login" >&2
  exit 2
}

export DATABASE_URL="postgres://${PG_USER}:${PG_PASSWORD}@127.0.0.1:${PORT}/${PG_DB}?sslmode=disable"
# A DB test that cannot see DATABASE_URL fails instead of skipping (CI sets this too).
export REQUIRE_CONTRACT=1

printf 'session-core DB tests: %s on 127.0.0.1:%s, database %s, container %s\n' \
  "$IMAGE" "$PORT" "$PG_DB" "$CONTAINER"

status=0
(
  cd "$RUST_DIR"
  # These two tests dial a provisioned NATS broker through NATS_URL, which this run does not set.
  cargo test -p session-core --bins -- "$@" --include-ignored --test-threads=1 \
    --skip outbox_drain_publishes_every_row_kind_through_a_provisioned_broker \
    --skip requeued_terminal_rows_are_delivered_once_the_cause_is_fixed
) || status=$?

if [[ "$status" -eq 0 ]]; then
  printf 'session-core DB tests: ok (the exit trap removes the container)\n'
else
  printf 'session-core DB tests: failed with exit %s (the exit trap removes the container)\n' "$status" >&2
fi
exit "$status"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Contract test for the disposable-Postgres harness. It starts no Docker and no
# cargo; it fails when the harness drifts from the rules it must keep.

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
HARNESS="$ROOT_DIR/scripts/tests/session-core-db-tests.sh"

test -f "$HARNESS"
if grep -q $'\r' "$HARNESS"; then
  echo 'harness must use LF line endings' >&2
  exit 1
fi

source_text="$(cat "$HARNESS")"
for required in \
  'postgres:16.14-alpine3.24' \
  '-p 127.0.0.1::5432' \
  'docker rm -f -v' \
  'trap cleanup EXIT' \
  'pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1' \
  'session_core_test' \
  'unset DATABASE_URL' \
  '--include-ignored' \
  '--test-threads=1' \
  'provisioned_broker'; do
  grep -F -- "$required" <<<"$source_text" >/dev/null || {
    echo "harness is missing required text: $required" >&2
    exit 1
  }
done

for forbidden in \
  'model-plane-postgres' \
  'docker compose' \
  'docker build' \
  'system prune' \
  'volume prune' \
  '--volumes' \
  'set -x' \
  'local-proof-only' \
  ' -P '; do
  if grep -F -- "$forbidden" <<<"$source_text" >/dev/null; then
    echo "harness must not contain: $forbidden" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

printf 'session-core DB test harness contract: ok\n'

# Docker Desktop recovery (Windows)

Owner: Model Plane operator. Script: `apps/Model Plane/scripts/dev/docker-desktop-recover.ps1` (a dry run unless `-Apply` is given).

Context: On 2026-10-17 the Docker Desktop VM wedged twice. The first time the backend log showed `connect tcp 192.168.65.7:2376: no route to host`. The second time the WSL VM load average was about 468 with 94 MB free, because dozens of `rustc` and `rust-lld` processes from an orphaned Rust build container were still running and no Windows process owned them. Each forced restart then failed on stale socket folders that Windows cannot delete (error 1920). The fix below worked on 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12. It renames the folders and never deletes them.

## Symptoms

- `docker` commands hang, or fail with a connection error.
- The Docker logs contain `no route to host` for 192.168.65.x:2376.
- A restart fails with `initializing Secrets Engine: listening on unix://...docker-secrets-engine\engine.sock: remove ...: The file cannot be accessed by the system`, or with `initializing Ingest server: ...Docker\run\sailor-ingest.sock: remove ...`.
- Container work stops, the VM load stays high, and free memory is low.

## Diagnose (read-only; every command has a time limit)

Run these in PowerShell 7. If a command hangs for more than about 30 seconds, press Ctrl+C and move on. A hang is itself a symptom.

1. Engine: `docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'`. No answer means the engine is down or wedged.
2. Processes: `Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.ProcessName -match '^(Docker Desktop|com\.docker\..+|vpnkit.*)$' } | Select-Object ProcessName, Id, StartTime`
3. Distro: `$env:WSL_UTF8 = '1'; wsl.exe -l -v`. Read the `docker-desktop` state. Do not start it just to look.
4. Only if it says Running: `wsl.exe -d docker-desktop --exec cat /proc/loadavg` and `wsl.exe -d docker-desktop --exec grep MemAvailable /proc/meminfo`. A load in the tens or hundreds, or MemAvailable under about 300 MB, means an overloaded VM.
5. Build processes in the VM, only if Running: `wsl.exe -d docker-desktop --exec sh -c "grep -l -x -E 'rustc|rust-lld|cargo' /proc/[0-9]*/comm 2>/dev/null | wc -l"`. A large count with no matching container is the orphan pattern.
6. Host free space: `Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select-Object Name, @{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB,1)}}`. The VM disk cannot grow when the host volume is full.
7. Logs: `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Docker\log') -Recurse -File -Filter '*.log' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 5`, then `Select-String -LiteralPath <file> -Pattern 'no route to host|initializing Secrets Engine|initializing Ingest server|error 1920|cannot be accessed by the system'`.
8. The script's dry run: `pwsh -NoProfile -File "apps/Model Plane/scripts/dev/docker-desktop-recover.ps1"`. It changes nothing. Exit 0 means the report is complete; exit 3 means Docker Desktop.exe was not found.

## Fix

1. Read the dry-run report. Check that the process names, the folder paths and the Docker Desktop.exe path are the ones you expect.
2. If the engine still answers and a build container is running, find that container first (see the orphan section) and stop it by ID. If the engine does not answer, skip this step; the restart stops the VM's processes.
3. Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File "apps/Model Plane/scripts/dev/docker-desktop-recover.ps1" -Apply`. Add `-Force` only if the engine answers but cannot be used, because step 2 of the script then stops every running container.
4. The script stops the Docker Desktop processes, terminates the `docker-desktop` distro, renames `%LOCALAPPDATA%\docker-secrets-engine` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Docker\run` to `*.stale-<timestamp>`, starts Docker Desktop, and waits up to five minutes for `docker info`.
5. Expect every container in the VM to stop. Named volumes survive. Containers with a restart policy return with the engine.
6. Restart the Model Plane stack with its launcher: `cd "apps/Model Plane" && ./scripts/compose.sh up -d`, as `apps/Model Plane/CLAUDE.md` says. The compose file header names `./build-verevon-services.sh --from model` for builds. Never use a bare `docker compose up`.
7. Delete the `*.stale-*` folders only after a working restart, by hand, on that exact path. They may need an elevated shell.

Manual equivalent, if the script is unavailable: quit Docker Desktop from the tray; `wsl.exe --terminate docker-desktop`; rename the two folders to `*.stale-<timestamp>`; start `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DockerDesktop\Docker Desktop.exe`; wait for `docker info`.

## If the engine still does not start

- Read the log lines the script printed. Do not reset.
- In an elevated PowerShell, check the Docker service with `Get-Service *docker*`. The script cannot stop a SYSTEM service without elevation, and it says so when that happens.
- Free host disk space before anything else if the host volume is near full.
- Escalate to the user. `wsl.exe --shutdown` stops every WSL distro, including unrelated work, so it needs the user's explicit approval.

## What not to do

- Do not click "Reset to factory defaults" in Docker Desktop. It deletes every container, image and volume, including the Postgres data of every plane.
- Do not run `wsl --unregister docker-desktop` or `wsl --unregister docker-desktop-data`, and do not delete the Docker Desktop WSL data folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Docker\wsl`.
- Do not run `docker system prune --volumes`, `docker volume prune` or `docker builder prune` as a recovery step. Volumes hold the database data, and prune on a full disk does not free space safely.
- Do not run `wsl.exe --shutdown` as the first step.
- Do not delete the stale socket folders. Rename them; Windows cannot remove their reparse points (error 1920).
- Do not start a detached Rust build container to run tests on this machine. Run cargo on the host, one crate at a time. Linux-only tests may run in a container only in the foreground, with `--rm`, a `--name` and a memory cap.

## How to spot an orphaned build container

An orphan keeps building or testing after the command that started it has exited.

- List: `docker ps --format "table {{.ID}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.RunningFor}}\t{{.Names}}"`. Suspects are `rust:*` images, names you do not recognise, no `com.docker.compose.project` label, and an age of hours with no matching terminal.
- Inspect: `docker inspect --format "{{.Config.Cmd}} {{.State.StartedAt}}" <id>`. A `cargo` or `sh -c "cargo ..."` command with no owner is an orphan.
- Find its process in the VM with the step 5 pattern, which prints the PID in the path, then show the command line: `wsl.exe -d docker-desktop --exec sh -c "tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/<pid>/cmdline"`.
- Stop only by ID, after inspect shows the command: `docker stop <id>`. Remove it with `docker rm <id>` only once you have decided its state can be lost. Never stop by image pattern, and never prune.

## Prevent recurrence

- The Model Plane plan tells people to run Linux-gated Rust tests in a `rust:1` container on Windows (`docs/plans/model-plane-chat-build-plan-2026-10-14.md`, lines 1106 and 2108). That is a likely origin of the orphan, not a confirmed one. Until those instructions carry limits, use the foreground form with `--rm`, a `--name` and `--memory`, and check `docker ps` afterwards.
- Run one Rust build at a time in the VM, and check `docker stats --no-stream` before starting another.
- The VM memory limit is a user setting (Docker Desktop, Settings, Resources; or `[wsl2] memory=` in `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig`). Scripts in this repo do not change it.

## Verify after recovery

- `docker info` answers with a server version.
- `docker ps` lists the expected stack containers.
- `wsl.exe -d docker-desktop --exec cat /proc/loadavg` shows a load near idle.
- `docker exec model-plane-postgres-1 pg_isready -U postgres` reports that it is accepting connections.

## 2026-10-17 - The chat UI reaches the agent route only in plan mode, so no UI run can reach an effectful tool, and an approved plan has no path to execution

**State:** `proposed`
(found 2026-10-17 while proving WS03 S5 on the stack; the fix is WS14 S2, plan approve-then-execute, which the build plan's spine text calls plan-continue; DEC-04; not built)

**The gap.** The chat "Do" control sends `plan_mode: true` together with the `agentic` feature. The SPA adds `agentic` only when plan mode is on (`apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/api/chat-client.ts:1085`), and it sends `plan_mode` from the same flag (`chat-client.ts:1117-1121`). model-gateway enters the agent route only for an `agentic` turn and forwards `plan_mode` into execution-core (`apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs:1450-1516` and `sse.rs:9047-9063`). execution-core pins a plan-mode run to `READ_ONLY` (`sse.rs:9027-9028`) and rejects, as a tool error and before dispatch, any call that `permission::is_risky_call` classifies as risky, or that is a restricted-context write (`apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:1845-1867`). So no UI run reaches a risky tool.

Approval does not close the gap. `approveTurnPlan` calls `approvePlan` and then sets the composer back to Ask (`apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/use-chat-controller.ts:2066-2077`). Ask is the plain-chat loop, which refuses side effects (`apps/Model Plane/CLAUDE.md`, Code Style). model-gateway consumes an approved plan only for a run that is not in plan mode (`sse.rs:9599-9603`), and no UI turn sends one. The only route that runs with `plan_mode` false, `/continue` (`sse.rs:13493-13507`), needs a granted approval for the run, and a plan-mode run does not create one for a risky call.

**The decision.** Plan approval starts a new Do run, which is not in plan mode and carries the granted rung and the approved plan (WS14 S2, DEC-04). The execute turn is sent at approval (`continuation: execute_now`), not left for the user to type, and the gateway binds the grant to that run. The planned ledger line is: Plan approval starts a new Do run; a grant never widens a run in flight. The names MODEL_GATEWAY_PLAN_EXECUTE_ON_APPROVE, BindGrantToRun and chat.execute_approved_plan are planned. None of them exists in the tree yet. The switch defaults off.

Until it ships, the UI cannot cause an effect. That is the safe state: the gap removes a feature and does not open a hole.

**Assumptions to re-check.** The no-effectful-tool statement holds only if `permission::is_risky_call` covers every effectful tool; the WS05 declared effect classes are the planned check. It also assumes that a plan-mode run which pauses for a non-risky tool cannot reach an effect through `/continue`. That path is not traced yet.

**Trigger to flip to `implemented`.** WS14 S2 is merged, MODEL_GATEWAY_PLAN_EXECUTE_ON_APPROVE is on in the proof stack, and a live run is recorded: one approval, one executed call under the granted rung, one terminal receipt, and a second approval click that executes nothing.

tests.name: session-core-db-tests-test.sh (contract, no Docker, no cargo)
tests.proves: The harness keeps the pinned image tag, loopback-only publish (-p 127.0.0.1::5432), EXIT-trap removal (docker rm -f -v), the TCP readiness probe, the session_core_test database, unset DATABASE_URL, --include-ignored and --test-threads=1, and the two NATS skips; it is LF-only and contains no stack-container reference, compose, build, prune, --volumes, set -x, -P or the old local-proof password.

tests.name: harness run, filter loop_checkpoint
tests.proves: S4 DB-backed loop checkpoint tests (compare-and-set save, claim lease, close, purge) pass on a disposable, freshly migrated database. The lead runs this when the Docker engine answers.

tests.name: harness run, filter tool_ledger
tests.proves: S5 reservation, finalize and sweep tests, including the reserved to unknown_outcome transition with closed_by = 'sweep', on the same disposable database.

tests.name: harness run, no filter
tests.proves: Every ignored session-core DB test runs; cargo's summary gives the count; the two NATS-only tests are excluded by name; afterwards `docker ps -a --filter name=session-core-dbtest` is empty.

tests.name: docker-desktop-recover.ps1 dry run
tests.proves: The script parses (PowerShell parses the whole file before running), reports processes, distro state, VM probe when Running, folders, exe location and log matches, exits 0 (or 3 when Docker Desktop.exe is absent), and %LOCALAPPDATA% listing is identical before and after.

tests.name: docker-desktop-recover.ps1 -Apply on a healthy engine
tests.proves: The guard refuses with exit 2, prints the -Force advice, and changes nothing. This is safe to run on a working machine.

tests.name: docker-desktop-recover.ps1 dry run with a missing -DockerDesktopExe path
tests.proves: Exit 3 with no state change, so the exe guard works before any apply step.

tests.name: bash -n on the harness
tests.proves: The shell script is syntactically valid before any run.

Create apps/Model Plane/scripts/dev/docker-desktop-recover.ps1 (ASCII). Run the dry run; expect exit 0, or exit 3 if Docker Desktop.exe is in another location. Confirm %LOCALAPPDATA% is unchanged. Run -Apply once on the healthy engine to confirm exit 2 and no change. Run the dry run with a bogus -DockerDesktopExe to confirm exit 3.

The lead commits, not this design. Suggested messages: `docs(model-plane): record the WS03 build ledger and the plan-mode gap`, and `chore(model-plane): add a disposable session-core DB harness and a Docker Desktop recovery runbook`. End each commit message with the Co-Authored-By line the session attribution rule specifies. Keep the untracked .plan-work/ folder out of the commit.
risks: Docker dependency: the harness's docker version, docker image inspect and docker run calls have no time bound, by design, because a coreutils timeout binary cannot be assumed on Git Bash PATH. On a wedged engine they can hang; the runbook is the fallback, and the operator should Ctrl+C and follow it.

The per-run password is visible in the docker run command line and in docker inspect of the container until it is removed. Acceptable for a loopback-only, disposable container with a random password; an --env-file would reduce this later.

If the trap is bypassed (kill -9, power loss), the container and its anonymous volume leak. The leak adds to the full-disk risk in the 2026-07 roadmap. Clean up by name only: docker ps -a --filter name=session-core-dbtest, then docker rm -f -v on those names.
--include-ignored also re-runs the non-DB unit tests, which costs time. CI uses --ignored with a filter. The brief's flag is kept; switching to --ignored is a one-word change.
The NATS skip is by test name. If those tests are renamed, the skip matches nothing and the tests fail loudly on the missing NATS_URL. A loud failure, not silent success.
The recovery script relies on Docker process names and the Docker Desktop.exe path, which the repository does not record. The dry run prints what it finds. Review it before -Apply.

Under -Apply, renaming a folder fails if a process still holds it. com.docker.service runs as SYSTEM and cannot be stopped without elevation. Step 3 then fails and nothing is deleted; the runbook says to use an elevated shell.
wsl --terminate docker-desktop stops every container in the VM, including other planes' stacks. Their named volumes survive, but those stacks must be restarted afterwards.

The gap entry is a code-reading finding. It depends on is_risky_call covering all effectful tools (WS05) and on the untraced /continue path for plan-mode pauses. It stays proposed until both are checked.
The S5 live proof has no artifact in the repository (grep for 2026-10-17 across apps/Model Plane/docs and docs/plans found nothing). The Build ledger line is a claim until the evidence is saved.

Observed, out of scope: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/store.rs:16 has a hardcoded default DATABASE_URL with postgres:postgres at localhost:5432. The harness always overrides DATABASE_URL, so this default does not affect it. Flagged for the owners.
The .plan-work/ folder is untracked and holds WS03 design notes; it must not be committed with these changes.

The compose header (line 3) names ./build-verevon-services.sh --from model for builds, while apps/Model Plane/CLAUDE.md names ./scripts/compose.sh up -d. The runbook names compose.sh for the restart and mentions both; the lead should confirm which launcher is current.
invariants: The harness never names, reads, or touches model-plane-postgres or any other container. It uses no -P, no compose, no build, no prune, and no volume removal except its own container's anonymous volume via docker rm -f -v on the generated name.
The harness never prints DATABASE_URL or the password, never enables set -x, and never uses a DATABASE_URL inherited from the shell.

The recovery script's dry run performs no state change. Under -Apply its only changes are stopping Docker Desktop process names, wsl --terminate docker-desktop, and two Rename-Item calls on exact named folders. It never calls unregister, shutdown, remove, or delete, and it refuses while the engine answers unless -Force is given.
New shell files are LF (.gitattributes *.sh eol=lf). The ledger working copy stays CRLF, the plan doc stays LF, and the PowerShell file is ASCII.
Ledger entries stay newest first, and no existing entry is edited. The 2026-10-16 entry stays proposed until its own trigger is met.
No new file reads or prints a credential, token, or DATABASE_URL, and none writes outside the worktree.
